title: Canonical scalar-restriction diagrams for the boundary comparison
statement:
Let $E,\Omega$ be normed fields with a normed $E$-algebra structure on $\Omega$, and let $c:C_E\to C_\Omega$ be the all-continuous coefficient inclusion [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Use ordinary tensor extension with its actual unit [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], and the canonical exact derived restriction $\operatorname{Res}$, pullback/restriction isomorphism and directional direct-image/restriction map [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-closed-base-change]. For $p\in\mathbf N$, a commutative ring $R$ and $t:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to R$, use the full tower $T$, stratum $S$, actual tests, sources, normalization, $\lambda$ and $\beta$ of [def-sfb-root-boundary-comparison]. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional $E$-space. For $K=E,\Omega$, canonically identify the chosen condensation model $M_K=\operatorname{model}(K,E,M)$ [def-sfb-derived-profinite-evaluation] with the all-continuous model of [lem-sfb-profinite-constant-derived-functions]: the isomorphism is uniquely characterized as the identity on every continuous-function section, using [lem-sfb-topological-module-condensation]. Transport the existing sectionwise map $E\otimes_E M\to\Omega\otimes_E M$ through these identifications to obtain $u_M:M_E\to\operatorname{Res}M_\Omega$, which is $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. For every supplied lisse $N$ on $T$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] and supplied $e:i^*N\cong p_S^*M_E$, set $N_\Omega=C_{\Omega,T}\otimes_{C_{E,T}}N$. There exists exactly one isomorphism $e_\Omega:i^*N_\Omega\cong p_S^*M_\Omega$ whose homomorphism, after exact scalar restriction and precomposition with the pulled ordinary tensor unit, is $e$ followed by the point pullback of $u_M$. Express this actual unit equation in degree zero, using the canonical exact derived pullback/restriction and point-pullback/restriction identifications. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding makes this equivalent to the ordinary unit equation and specifies the ordinary isomorphism itself. Its construction is the canonical ordinary pullback/extension isomorphism followed by ordinary tensor extension of $e$ and the finite-free continuous-model identification; the extension/restriction adjunction gives uniqueness. This includes rank zero and incomplete $\Omega$. Neither the Omega-model nor its identification is an independent parameter.

For every profinite $P$, put $J=\operatorname{Res}(M_\Omega[0])$, $H=p_S^*R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{C_E}(C_E[P],J)$ and $D=R\rho_{P,*}p_{S[P]}^*J$, with canonical evaluation $\beta_J:H\to D$. The target unit $u_H:T_E\to H$ is derived internal Hom applied to the actual $u_M[0]$. The target restriction $r_H:\operatorname{Res}T_\Omega\to H$ is the inverse point-pullback/restriction identification followed by the existing directional derived internal-Hom restriction [lem-sfb-profinite-constant-derived-functions]. Put $A=s^*Rq_{P,*}N_P[0]$, $B=\operatorname{Res}(s^*Rq_{P,*}N_{\Omega,P}[0])$, and $C=s^*Rq_{P,*}\operatorname{Res}(N_{\Omega,P}[0])$. The cospan $A\xrightarrow{a}C\xleftarrow{b}B$ uses, respectively, the actual pulled ordinary tensor unit, and the canonical pullback/restriction identification followed by directional direct-image/restriction. Let $d:C\to D$ be the E-boundary exchange on the restricted Omega-test module, followed by canonical pullback/restriction, the pullback of exactly $e_\Omega$, and point-pullback/restriction. Define ScalarCompatibility to assert, for every such $M,N,e,P$ and both normalized comparison isomorphisms $\alpha_E,\alpha_\Omega$ with these fixed data, the single equality of morphisms from $A\oplus B$ to the common object $D$:
$$[\lambda_E\alpha_Eu_H\beta_J,\;\operatorname{Res}(\lambda_\Omega\alpha_\Omega)r_H\beta_J]=[a,b]\,d.$$
Here brackets denote the biproduct descendent, so this is exactly the two commuting legs of the canonical scalar cospan. Both comparisons meet the same restricted Omega-model through the actual model unit. No directional direct-image/restriction comparison is inverted and no scalar-extension/direct-image isomorphism is assumed. Rank zero, the empty parameter and incomplete Omega are included.
